I say, Holmes, you must confess that you cut it rather fine. It was all we could do to overhaul her. All is well that ends well. But I certainly did not know that the _Aurora_ was such a clipper. Smith says she is one of the fastest launches on the river, and that if he had had another man to help him with the engines we should never have caught her. He swears he knew nothing of this Norwood business.

events.label: Jonathan Small contradicts about Smith's knowledge and says he chose the launch because it was fast

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: Neither he did, cried our prisoner,—not a word. I chose his launch because I heard that she was a flier. We told him nothing, but we paid him well, and he was to get something handsome if we reached our vessel, the _Esmeralda_, at Gravesend, outward bound for the Brazils.

events.label: Athelney Jones says they will see no wrong comes to Smith if he did no wrong and they will be quick to catch men but not quick to condemn

communicates.speaker: athelney_jones
communicates.content: Well, if he has done no wrong we shall see that no wrong comes to him. If we are pretty quick in catching our men, we are not so quick in condemning them.

events.label: Athelney Jones announces they will be at Vauxhall Bridge and says they will land Dr. Watson with the treasure-box

communicates.speaker: athelney_jones
communicates.content: We will be at Vauxhall Bridge presently, and shall land you, Dr. Watson, with the treasure-box.

events.label: Athelney Jones states he is taking grave responsibility and that an agreement is an agreement

communicates.speaker: athelney_jones
communicates.content: I need hardly tell you that I am taking a very grave responsibility upon myself in doing this. It is most irregular; but of course an agreement is an agreement.

events.label: Athelney Jones says he will send an inspector with Dr. Watson due to the value of the charge

communicates.speaker: athelney_jones
communicates.content: I must, however, as a matter of duty, send an inspector with you, since you have so valuable a charge.

events.label: Athelney Jones asks if Dr. Watson will drive; Dr. Watson agrees

communicates.speaker: athelney_jones
communicates.content: You will drive, no doubt?

events.label: Dr. Watson says yes, he will drive

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
communicates.content: Yes, I shall drive.

events.label: Athelney Jones asks where the key is; Jonathan Small says it is at the bottom of the river

communicates.speaker: athelney_jones
communicates.content: It is a pity there is no key, that we may make an inventory first. You will have to break it open. Where is the key, my man?

events.label: Jonathan Small answers that the key is at the bottom of the river

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: At the bottom of the river

events.label: Athelney Jones instructs Dr. Watson to be careful and bring the box back to the Baker Street rooms

communicates.speaker: athelney_jones
communicates.content: However, doctor, I need not warn you to be careful. Bring the box back with you to the Baker Street rooms. You will find us there, on our way to the station.

events.label: Dr. Watson is landed at Vauxhall with his iron box and an inspector accompanies him
After a drive, Dr. Watson arrives at Mrs. Cecil Forrester's house
Dr. Watson goes to the drawing-room with the box and leaves the inspector in the cab
Miss Morstan rises when Dr. Watson enters and asks what news he brought

communicates.speaker: mary_morstan
communicates.content: I heard a cab drive up. I thought that Mrs. Forrester had come back very early, but I never dreamed that it might be you. What news have you brought me?

events.label: Dr. Watson tells Mary Morstan he has brought something better than news and announces he has brought her a fortune

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
communicates.content: I have brought something better than news. I have brought you a fortune.

events.label: Mary Morstan asks whether the treasure is in the iron box

communicates.speaker: mary_morstan
communicates.content: Is that the treasure, then?

events.label: Dr. Watson says the box is the great Agra treasure and states the division and amounts

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
communicates.content: Yes, this is the great Agra treasure. Half of it is yours and half is Thaddeus Sholto’s. You will have a couple of hundred thousand each. Think of that! An annuity of ten thousand pounds. There will be few richer young ladies in England. Is it not glorious?

events.label: Dr. Watson claims the box has been won through Holmes's clue work and says they nearly lost it at the last moment

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
communicates.content: No, no, not to me, but to my friend Sherlock Holmes. With all the will in the world, I could never have followed up a clue which has taxed even his analytical genius. As it was, we very nearly lost it at the last moment.

events.label: Mary Morstan tells Dr. Watson to sit down and tell her all about it

communicates.speaker: mary_morstan
communicates.content: Pray sit down and tell me all about it, Dr. Watson,

events.label: Dr. Watson narrates the events since he had last seen Mary Morstan
Mary Morstan reacts to the dart narrowly missing them and is provided with water

communicates.speaker: mary_morstan
communicates.content: It is nothing. I am all right again. It was a shock to me to hear that I had placed my friends in such horrible peril.

events.label: Dr. Watson says there will be no more gloomy details and points to the treasure

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
communicates.content: That is all over. It was nothing. I will tell you no more gloomy details. Let us turn to something brighter. There is the treasure. What could be brighter than that? I got leave to bring it with me, thinking that it would interest you to be the first to see it.

events.label: Mary Morstan examines the box and asks about the key

communicates.speaker: mary_morstan
communicates.content: What a pretty box! This is Indian work, I suppose? Where is the key?

events.label: Dr. Watson says Small threw the key into the Thames and borrows Mrs. Forrester’s poker to open the hasp

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
communicates.content: Small threw it into the Thames.

events.label: Dr. Watson opens the box lid and Mary Morstan and Dr. Watson look inside in astonishment
The iron box is found empty
Mary Morstan says the treasure is lost

communicates.speaker: mary_morstan
communicates.content: The treasure is lost.

events.label: Dr. Watson and Mary Morstan react verbally with 'Thank God' after the treasure is removed

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
communicates.content: Thank God!

events.label: Dr. Watson states he can tell Mary Morstan how he loves her now that the treasure is gone

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
communicates.content: Because you are within my reach again. Because I love you, Mary, as truly as ever a man loved a woman. Because this treasure, these riches, sealed my lips. Now that they are gone I can tell you how I love you. That is why I said, ‘Thank God.’

events.label: Mary Morstan says 'Thank God' too and Dr. Watson draws her to his side

communicates.speaker: mary_morstan
communicates.content: Then I say, ‘Thank God,’ too,

events.label: Dr. Watson notes that someone who had lost a treasure has gained one that night
The inspector receives an empty box from the narrator
The inspector says the reward is gone

communicates.speaker: inspector
communicates.content: “There goes the reward!”

events.label: The inspector tells that without money there is no pay and that the night’s work would have been worth a tenner each

communicates.speaker: inspector
communicates.content: “Where there is no money there is no pay. This night’s work would have been worth a tenner each to Sam Brown and me if the treasure had been there.”

events.label: The narrator says Mr. Thaddeus Sholto is rich and will reward them

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
communicates.content: “Mr. Thaddeus Sholto is a rich man,” I said. “He will see that you are rewarded, treasure or no.”

events.label: The inspector shakes his head despondently
The inspector says it is a bad job and that Mr. Athelney Jones will think so

communicates.speaker: inspector
communicates.content: “It’s a bad job,” he repeated; “and so Mr. Athelney Jones will think.”

events.label: The detective looks blank when the narrator shows the empty box at Baker Street
Holmes, the prisoner, and Athelney Jones arrive at Baker Street and change plans to report at a station on the way
The narrator exhibits the empty box to Small
Small leans back in his chair and laughs aloud
Athelney Jones angrily says Small did this

communicates.speaker: athelney_jones
communicates.content: “This is your doing, Small,” said Athelney Jones, angrily.

events.label: Small claims he put the treasure away so that Athelney Jones cannot take it

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “Yes, I have put it away where you shall never lay hand upon it,” he cried, exultantly.

events.label: Small declares it is his treasure and that if he cannot have the loot he will ensure no one else does

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “It is my treasure; and if I can’t have the loot I’ll take darned good care that no one else does. I tell you that no living man has any right to it, unless it is three men who are in the Andaman convict-barracks and myself.”

events.label: Small says he knows he cannot use the treasure and that those three men cannot either

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “I know now that I cannot have the use of it, and I know that they cannot.”

events.label: Small says he acted for them as much as for himself and calls it the sign of four

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “I have acted all through for them as much as for myself. It’s been the sign of four with us always.”

events.label: Small says he knows they would have thrown the treasure into the Thames and not let it go to Sholto or Morstan’s relatives

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “Well I know that they would have had me do just what I have done, and throw the treasure into the Thames rather than let it go to kith or kin of Sholto or of Morstan.”

events.label: Small says it was not to make them rich that they did for Achmet

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “It was not to make them rich that we did for Achmet.”

events.label: Small says the treasure is where the key is and where little Tonga is

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “You’ll find the treasure where the key is, and where little Tonga is.”

events.label: Small says that when he saw his launch must catch them, he put the loot away in a safe place and that there are no rupees for this journey

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “When I saw that your launch must catch us, I put the loot away in a safe place. There are no rupees for you this journey.”

events.label: Athelney Jones says Small is deceiving them

communicates.speaker: athelney_jones
communicates.content: “You are deceiving us, Small,” said Athelney Jones, sternly.

events.label: Small answers that throwing the treasure into the Thames would have been easier if he threw the box as well

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “If you had wished to throw the treasure into the Thames it would have been easier for you to have thrown box and all.”

events.label: Small claims it would have been easier for him to throw and for Athelney Jones to recover and looks shrewdly

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “Easier for me to throw, and easier for you to recover,” he answered, with a shrewd, sidelong look.

events.label: Small tells that whoever hunted him down could pick an iron box from the bottom of a river

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “The man that was clever enough to hunt me down is clever enough to pick an iron box from the bottom of a river.”

events.label: Small says that since the men are scattered over miles, it may be a harder job

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “Now that they are scattered over five miles or so, it may be a harder job.”

events.label: Small says it went to his heart to do it and that he was half mad when he came up with them

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “It went to my heart to do it, though. I was half mad when you came up with us.”

events.label: Small says there is no good grieving over it and uses an idiom about spilled milk

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “However, there’s no good grieving over it. I’ve had ups in my life, and I’ve had downs, but I’ve learned not to cry over spilled milk.”

events.label: The detective says the matter is very serious and that Small thwarted justice

communicates.speaker: detective
communicates.content: “This is a very serious matter, Small,” said the detective. “If you had helped justice, instead of thwarting it in this way, you would have had a better chance at your trial.”

events.label: Small snarls and challenges the idea of justice by asking whose loot it is and where justice is

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “Justice!” snarled the ex-convict. “A pretty justice! Whose loot is this, if it is not ours? Where is the justice that I should give it up to those who have never earned it?”

events.label: Small says he earned the Agra treasure and describes twenty years of imprisonment under harsh conditions

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “Look how I have earned it! Twenty long years in that fever-ridden swamp, all day at work under the mangrove-tree, all night chained up in the filthy convict-huts, bitten by mosquitoes, racked with ague, bullied by every cursed black-faced policeman who loved to take it out of a white man. That was how I earned the Agra treasure; and you talk to me of justice because I cannot bear to feel that I have paid this price only that another may enjoy it!”

events.label: Small says he would rather be hanged or be hit by Tonga’s darts than live in a convict’s cell while another enjoys the money

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “I would rather swing a score of times, or have one of Tonga’s darts in my hide, than live in a convict’s cell and feel that another man is at his ease in a palace with the money that should be mine.”

events.label: Small drops his mask of stoicism and handcuffs clank as he speaks intensely
Holmes tells Small that they know nothing of his story and that they cannot say how far justice was originally on his side

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “You forget that we know nothing of all this,” said Holmes quietly. “We have not heard your story, and we cannot tell how far justice may originally have been on your side.”

events.label: Small says Holmes has been fair-spoken, but that Small can thank him for his bracelets

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “Well, sir, you have been very fair-spoken to me, though I can see that I have you to thank that I have these bracelets upon my wrists.”

events.label: Small says he bears no grudge and that it is fair and above-board

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “Still, I bear no grudge for that. It is all fair and above-board.”

events.label: Small offers to tell his story if Holmes wants to hear it, saying he has no wish to hold it back

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “If you want to hear my story I have no wish to hold it back.”

events.label: Small says what he says is God’s truth

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “What I say to you is God’s truth, every word of it.”

events.label: Small asks Holmes to place the glass beside him and says he will put his lips to it if he is dry

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “Thank you; you can put the glass beside me here, and I’ll put my lips to it if I am dry.”

events.label: Small identifies himself as born near Pershore and says he would have many Smalls living there but doubts they would be glad to see him

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: “I am a Worcestershire man myself,—born near Pershore. I dare say you would find a heap of Smalls living there now if you were to look. I have often thought of taking a look round there, but the truth is that I was never much of a credit to the family, and I doubt if they would be so very glad to see me.”

events.label: Small says that at age about eighteen he joined the 3rd Buffs and started for India after taking the Queen’s shilling
Small says he went swimming in the Ganges and was taken by a crocodile, which nipped off his right leg above the knee
John Holder catches Small and paddles to the bank after Small is taken by the crocodile
Small is in hospital for five months and later limps out with a timber toe strapped to his stump
Abel White hires Small as an overseer for indigo plantations
The great mutiny breaks out without warning
Small discovers Dawson’s wife and later Dawson dead during the mutiny
Small sees smoke and flames from Abel White’s bungalow
Small breaks away across the paddy-fields and reaches safety within the walls at Agra late at night
A volunteer corps of clerks and merchants is formed and Small joins it
Small is instructed to take charge during certain hours of the night of a small isolated door on the southwest side of the fort at Agra
Two Sikh troopers are placed under Small’s command
Small is instructed to fire his musket if anything goes wrong to rely upon help from the central guard

communicates.speaker: officer
communicates.content: “...I was instructed if anything went wrong to fire my musket, when I might rely upon help coming at once from the central guard.”

events.label: Small keeps watch for two nights with Mahomet Singh and Abdullah Khan
At two in the morning, the rounds pass and Small tries to strike a match by taking out his pipe
The two Sikhs seize Small instantly after he strikes a match
One Sikh snatches Small’s firelock and levels it at his head while the other holds a knife to Small’s throat and threatens to plunge it if he moves
Mahomet Singh or Abdullah Khan whispers to Small not to make a noise and says the fort is safe enough and there are no rebel dogs on this side of the river

communicates.speaker: mahomet_singh
communicates.content: “Don’t make a noise. The fort is safe enough. There are no rebel dogs on this side of the river.”

events.label: Small waits in silence to see what the men want from him
Abdullah Khan tells Sahib Abdullah Khan is the taller and fiercer of two men called Abdullah Khan and demands a choice

communicates.speaker: abdullah_khan
communicates.content: ‘You must either be with us now or you must be silenced forever... Which is it to be, death or life? We can only give you three minutes to decide, for the time is passing, and all must be done before the rounds come again.’

events.label: Abdullah Khan threatens throwing Sahib's body into a ditch if he refuses

communicates.speaker: abdullah_khan
communicates.content: ‘Either you are heart and soul with us on your oath on the cross of the Christians, or your body this night shall be thrown into the ditch and we shall pass over to our brothers in the rebel army. There is no middle way.’

events.label: Sahib asks how he can decide what Abdullah Khan wants

communicates.speaker: i
communicates.content: ‘How can I decide?’ ... ‘You have not told me what you want of me.’

events.label: Sahib refuses any action against the fort and tells Abdullah Khan to drive home his knife

communicates.speaker: i
communicates.content: ‘But I tell you now that if it is anything against the safety of the fort I will have no truck with it, so you can drive home your knife and welcome.’

events.label: Abdullah Khan claims the request is nothing against the fort and demands Sahib be rich

communicates.speaker: abdullah_khan
communicates.content: ‘It is nothing against the fort... We only ask you to do that which your countrymen come to this land for. We ask you to be rich.’

events.label: Abdullah Khan offers Sahib a quarter of the treasure if he swears oaths on a knife

communicates.speaker: abdullah_khan
communicates.content: ‘If you will be one of us this night, we will swear to you upon the naked knife... that you shall have your fair share of the loot. A quarter of the treasure shall be yours. We can say no fairer.’

events.label: Sahib asks what the treasure is

communicates.speaker: i
communicates.content: ‘But what is the treasure, then?’

events.label: Abdullah Khan demands Sahib swear by family and faith to raise no hand or speak against them

communicates.speaker: abdullah_khan
communicates.content: ‘You will swear, then,’ said he, ‘by the bones of your father, by the honour of your mother, by the cross of your faith, to raise no hand and speak no word against us, either now or afterwards?’

events.label: Sahib agrees to swear conditional on the fort not being endangered

communicates.speaker: i
communicates.content: ‘I will swear it,’ I answered, ‘provided that the fort is not endangered.’

events.label: Abdullah Khan adjusts division of treasure to include Dost Akbar and says four men will divide a quarter share

communicates.speaker: abdullah_khan
communicates.content: ‘Then my comrade and I will swear that you shall have a quarter of the treasure which shall be equally divided among the four of us.’ ... ‘No; Dost Akbar must have his share.’

events.label: Abdullah Khan tells Mahomet Singh to stand at the gate and give notice of the coming of the other men

communicates.speaker: abdullah_khan
communicates.content: ‘Do you stand at the gate, Mahomet Singh, and give notice of their coming.’

events.label: Abdullah Khan explains plan involving the merchant Achmet and Dost Akbar leading him to a side-postern

communicates.speaker: abdullah_khan
communicates.content: Abdullah Khan says a rajah in northern provinces hoards wealth, sends precious stones and pearls via a trusty servant to the fort at Agra under the disguise of a merchant named Achmet; that Achmet is in Agra with travelling companion Dost Akbar; that Dost Akbar will lead Achmet to a side-postern of the fort this night where Mahomet Singh and Abdullah Khan will await; that no one shall know of Achmet’s coming; and that the merchant Achmet will be eliminated from the world while the great treasure is divided among them.

events.label: Sahib describes deciding to join Abdullah Khan and receives back his firelock

communicates.speaker: i
communicates.content: ‘I am with you heart and soul,’ said I.

events.label: Abdullah Khan says they only have to wait for his brother and the merchant and explains his brother knows the plan

communicates.speaker: abdullah_khan
communicates.content: ‘We have now only to wait for my brother and the merchant.’ ... ‘The plan is his. He has devised it.’

events.label: Abdullah Khan says they will go to the gate and share the watch with Mahomet Singh

communicates.speaker: abdullah_khan
communicates.content: ‘We will go to the gate and share the watch with Mahomet Singh.’

events.label: Sahib challenges two arriving figures at the gate after uncovering his lantern

communicates.speaker: i
communicates.content: ‘Who goes there?’

events.label: Sahib uncovers lantern and receives name and plea from the merchant Achmet asking protection

communicates.speaker: achmet_merchant
communicates.content: ‘Your protection, Sahib... for the unhappy merchant Achmet... I have travelled across Rajpootana that I might seek the shelter of the fort at Agra. I have been robbed and beaten and abused because I have been the friend of the Company. It is a blessed night this when I am once more in safety,—I and my poor possessions.’

events.label: Sahib asks what is in the bundle and Achmet says it contains an iron box with family matters

communicates.speaker: i
communicates.content: ‘What have you in the bundle?’

events.label: Achmet offers to reward Sahib and his governor for shelter requested

communicates.speaker: achmet_merchant
communicates.content: ‘Yet I am not a beggar; and I shall reward you, young Sahib, and your governor also, if he will give me the shelter I ask.’

events.label: Sahib orders the Sikhs to take Achmet to the main guard

communicates.speaker: i
communicates.content: ‘Take him to the main guard,’ said I.

events.label: Achmet is moved through the dark gateway while Sahib remains at the gateway with a lantern
Voices and scuffle occur and Sahib sees Achmet running back, chased by the Sikh who attacks with a knife
Sahib shoots Achmet with his firelock as he races past and then watches Achmet killed by the Sikh
The narrator holds out his manacled hands for whiskey-and-water and then describes past events of carrying Achmet and burying him under loose bricks
Achmet is left buried in a natural grave formed by a sunken earth floor in a great empty hall
The group returns to a treasure chest, opens it, and displays and lists the gems inside
The group puts the gems back into the chest and carries the box to the gateway to show to Mahomet Singh
The four men renew an oath to keep their secret and agree to conceal the loot until the country is at peace
The treasure box is carried into a hall where the body had been buried and concealed under bricks in a wall hollow
The men draw plans and mark the sign of the four on them
The men are arrested as the murderers of Achmet after hopes of peace and plunder division
The narrator explains how a second servant spies on Achmet and leads to discovery of the body and charges of murder

communicates.speaker: i
communicates.content: ‘It came about in this way... He followed him like his shadow... He followed him that night... But could find no trace of Achmet... he spoke... to a sergeant of guides, who brought it to the ears of the commandant... A thorough search was quickly made, and the body was discovered... seized and brought to trial on a charge of murder,—three of us because we had held the gate that night, and the fourth because he was known to have been in the company of the murdered man.’

events.label: The three Sikhs receive penal servitude for life and the narrator is sentenced to death then commuted
Jonathan Small is transferred from Agra to Madras and then to Blair Island in the Andamans
Jonathan Small receives a hut in Hope Town and is left to himself
Jonathan Small is located in the surgery next to Dr. Somerton’s sitting-room
Jonathan Small turns out the lamp in the surgery and stands there to hear talk and watch playing
Dr. Somerton and other officers gather in Dr. Somerton’s rooms to play cards in the evening
Major Sholto loses money repeatedly at cards over multiple nights
Major Sholto and Captain Morstan arrive at Jonathan Small’s hut on the way to their quarters one night
Major Sholto says he has to send in his papers and that he is a ruined man as he passes Jonathan Small’s hut

communicates.speaker: major_sholto
communicates.content: It’s all up, Morstan, I shall have to send in my papers. I am a ruined man.

events.label: Jonathan Small speaks to Major Sholto on the beach a couple of days later asking for advice

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: I wish to have your advice, major.

events.label: Jonathan Small asks who is the proper person for hidden treasure to be handed over and states he knows its location

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: I wanted to ask you, sir, who is the proper person to whom hidden treasure should be handed over. I know where half a million worth lies, and, as I cannot use it myself, I thought perhaps the best thing that I could do would be to hand it over to the proper authorities, and then perhaps they would get my sentence shortened for me.

events.label: Major Sholto receives the information about half a million in jewels and pearls and responds that it should go to government

communicates.speaker: major_sholto
communicates.content: To government, Small—to government.

events.label: Jonathan Small asks whether he should give the information to the Governor-General

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: You think, then, sir, that I should give the information to the Governor-General?

events.label: Major Sholto warns Jonathan Small not to do anything rash and asks for the facts

communicates.speaker: major_sholto
communicates.content: Well, well, you must not do anything rash, or that you might repent. Let me hear all about it, Small. Give me the facts.

events.label: Major Sholto tells Jonathan Small to keep quiet and says he will see him again soon after the full story is told

communicates.speaker: major_sholto
communicates.content: This is a very important matter, Small. You must not say a word to any one about it, and I shall see you again soon.

events.label: Major Sholto and Captain Morstan come to Jonathan Small’s hut at night with a lantern and ask him to repeat the story
Captain Morstan acknowledges the story by stating he nods that it rings true enough to act upon

communicates.speaker: major_sholto
communicates.content: It rings true, eh? It’s good enough to act upon?

events.label: Major Sholto offers to involve Jonathan Small privately and asks what price he would ask

communicates.speaker: major_sholto
communicates.content: We have been talking it over, my friend here and I, and we have come to the conclusion that this secret of yours is hardly a government matter, after all, but is a private concern of your own, which of course you have the power of disposing of as you think best. Now, the question is, what price would you ask for it?

events.label: Jonathan Small proposes that the deal requires help for his freedom and his three companions’ freedom in exchange for a partnership with a fifth share

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: There is only one bargain which a man in my position can make. I shall want you to help me to my freedom, and to help my three companions to theirs. We shall then take you into partnership, and give you a fifth share to divide between you.

events.label: Jonathan Small states that escape requires a boat fit for voyage and provisions, and instructs them to bring a yacht

communicates.speaker: jonathan_small
communicates.content: The only bar to our escape is that we can get no boat fit for the voyage, and no provisions to last us for so long a time. There are plenty of little yachts and yawls at Calcutta or Madras which would serve our turn well. Do you bring one over. We shall engage to get aboard her by night, and if you will drop us on any part of the Indian coast you will have done your part of the bargain.

events.label: Major Sholto proposes testing the truth of Jonathan Small’s story by going back to India in the monthly relief-boat

communicates.speaker: major_sholto

events.label: Sherlock Holmes describes Mary Morstan as charming and useful for their work

events.label: Sherlock Holmes contrasts love with cold reason

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “But love is an emotional thing, and whatever is emotional is opposed to that true cold reason which I place above all things.”

events.label: Narrator contrasts alternating laziness with fits of energy

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: “I often think of those lines of old Goethe,—Schade dass die Natur nur _einen_ Mensch aus Dir schuf, Denn zum würdigen Mann war und zum Schelmen der Stoff.”

communicates.content: “By the way, _à propos_ of this Norwood business, you see that they had, as I surmised, a confederate in the house, who could be none other than Lal Rao, the butler: so Jones actually has the undivided honour of having caught one fish in his great haul.”

events.label: Narrator remarks that the division seems unfair

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
communicates.content: “The division seems rather unfair,”

events.label: Narrator says Sherlock Holmes did not get work but got a wife while Jones got credit

communicates.speaker: dr_john_watson
